back: People who live by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants, rather than farming or herding (e.g. the San).
People whose way of life depends mainly on keeping livestock such as cattle and sheep (e.g. the Khoikhoi).
A small group of related families who live and move together; the main unit of San society.
Moving from place to place with the seasons, following food, water or grazing.

front: Where is the richest collection of rock art in Zimbabwe?
back: The Matobo Hills (Matabeleland South), a World Heritage Site since 2003.
Bow and poisoned arrows; digging stick (sometimes weighted with a bored stone); ostrich eggshell water containers.

front: Why did the San have no chiefs?
back: Bands were small, owned little property and moved often, so decisions were made by discussion, guided by elders.

front: Why was sharing food important to the San?
back: A hunt did not succeed every day; sharing meant every family ate and kept the band united.

front: Name four parts of the San heritage.
back: Rock art; knowledge of plants and medicines; hunting and tool-making skills; tanning skins.
